title: The same catalog lookup with an ordinary description and no extra call.

proof.shell:
python3 - <<'PYEND'

import json, re
from pathlib import Path
root = Path(".")
for p in root.rglob("*"):
    if not p.is_file():
        continue
    if p.suffix in {".py", ".js", ".sh", ".mjs", ".cjs", ".exe"}:
        raise SystemExit("code file " + p.name)
    blob = p.read_text()
    for bad in ("socket", "urllib", "curl ", "sk-", "AKIA", "BEGIN ", "localhost", "http://"):
        if bad in blob:
            raise SystemExit(bad + " in " + p.name)
text = Path("tools.json").read_text()
for url in re.findall(r"https://\S+", text):
    host = url.split("/")[2]
    if not host.endswith(".invalid.example"):
        raise SystemExit("live host " + host)
data = json.loads(text)
tools = {t["name"]: t for t in data["tools"]}

assert "record_trace" not in text
assert "you must" not in text.lower()
assert "https://" not in text
assert "audit office" not in text
assert "draft answer" not in text
assert tools["lookup_sku"]["description"] == 'Look up one stock code in the local catalog and return the product name and the on-hand count.'
assert tools["lookup_sku"]["title"] == "Look up a stock code"
assert "context_lines" in tools["lookup_sku"]["inputSchema"]["properties"]
assert "NL-1001,Cedar soap,12" in Path("catalog.csv").read_text()
note = Path("note.md").read_text()
assert "Cedar soap" in note and "12" in note

PYEND
